seoDescription: Custom clear stickers printed on transparent vinyl or PET with white ink behind the colors. Glass, bottles, laptops and windows, in any shape from 100 pieces.
tagline: Transparent vinyl with white ink under the art, so only your design shows on glass or dark surfaces.
quickAnswer: Custom clear stickers are printed on transparent vinyl or polyester film, with a white ink layer laid under the colors where you want them solid and nothing printed where you want the surface to show through. They suit glass bottles, jars, windows, laptops and dark packaging. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, produced in 5 to 7 business days after proof approval.

sections.h2: Why the background disappears, and what the die cut clear page adds
sections.html:
Will the sticker show a white edge around my logo on a glass bottle? That is the question that brings most buyers to clear stickers, and the answer is no. We print on a transparent film, so anywhere the artwork is empty you see the bottle, the window or the laptop lid behind it. Your logo floats on the surface instead of sitting on a white rectangle.

This page covers clear material in all the shapes we cut: squares and circles trimmed to size, kiss cut sheets, rolls for an applicator, and contour cuts. If you already know you want the sticker cut tight to an irregular outline, the die cut clear sticker page deals with the border and cutting questions that come up on complex shapes. Think of this as the material page and that one as the shape page.

Clear decals and transparent stickers are the same product under different names; the trade calls them clear labels when they go on bottles.

sections.h2: White ink: the part of a clear sticker nobody tells you about
sections.html:
CMYK ink is translucent. Print yellow straight onto clear film and stick it on a brown bottle, and the yellow turns muddy because the brown shows through. The fix is a layer of white ink printed first, exactly under the areas you want opaque. We build that white layer for you from the artwork and show it on the proof as a separate view.

You can also ask for no white at all. Pale, airy designs on a light wall or a white candle jar look like they were printed on the object itself.

sections.h2: Surfaces and conditions clear vinyl was made for
sections.html:
Clear vinyl carries the same acrylic adhesive as the white vinyl across our custom sticker catalog and is rated for the same 3 to 5 years outdoors when laminated. It is 2 to 4 mil thick depending on the run, flexible enough to wrap a 2-inch diameter bottle without creasing.

  • Glass bottles and jars for beverages, candles, cosmetics and sauces, including cold and condensation-prone fridge products.
  • Laptops, phone cases, tumblers and water bottles where a white border would look like a price tag.
  • Storefront glass for hours, logos and promotions, up to 24 x 36 inches in one piece.
  • Clear or dark product packaging, where only the printed art should be visible.
  • Equipment and dashboards, as clear decals that do not hide the finish underneath.

Matte clear is worth knowing about. It kills the reflection, which helps on a window in direct sun, but it frosts the surface slightly, so the no-background effect is weaker than with gloss. For bottles we almost always recommend gloss.

sections.h2: Applying a clear sticker without trapping bubbles or dust
sections.html:
Clear stickers are less forgiving than white ones. Every speck of dust and every bubble shows, because there is no opaque print to hide it. The method below is what we tell customers who are hand-applying hundreds of bottles.

  1. Wipe the surface with isopropyl alcohol on a lint-free cloth and let it flash off. No glass cleaner; it leaves a film.
  2. Peel the sticker from the liner by bending the liner, not by picking at the sticker edge with a fingernail.
  3. Hold it by the edges, line it up, and lay down the middle first.
  4. Press outward from the center with a credit card or a felt squeegee, in overlapping strokes.
  5. If a bubble remains, prick it with a pin and press the air out toward the hole. It will vanish within a day.

For storefront glass over 12 inches, mist the glass with water plus one drop of dish soap, position the sticker, then squeegee the water out. The adhesive sets once the water is gone.

sections.h2: Ordering clear stickers in small counts, and how the price moves
sections.html:
A lot of searches for clear stickers come from makers who want a handful. Our floor is 100 pieces per design, and at that count you are paying from $0.30 each with free FedEx delivery in the United States, so a first run for a product launch costs less than a tank of gas. Several designs can share one order as long as each meets the 100 count.

From 500 pieces up, the per-sticker price falls fast because the white ink pass and the cut file are set up once. Roll format brings the unit cost lower still for anyone labeling with a hand dispenser, and we trim rolls to the core size your applicator takes. If clear turns out not to be the right base for your job, the stickers by material category compares every film and paper we print on, with the same 100-piece floor across all of them.

sections.h2: Clear, holographic or white vinyl: picking the base for a product label
sections.html:
Clear wins when the container is part of the look, as it is with a glass bottle of hot sauce or a clear cosmetic jar. White vinyl wins when you need the label itself to be bright on a dark bottle and you want the cleanest color accuracy, since every color sits on a true white base. Holographic film is the third choice when the package needs to catch light on a shelf; our custom holographic stickers use the same white-ink technique over a rainbow base, so colors stay readable while the unprinted areas shimmer.

Two things to avoid on clear. Very thin white type, under about 6 point, can look gray because the white ink layer is slightly narrower than the printed edge. And large unprinted gaps between elements should be kiss cut as one sheet rather than left as a floating film, or the sticker becomes hard to handle. We flag both on the proof.

faqs.q: Are custom clear stickers completely transparent where nothing is printed?
faqs.a: Yes with gloss clear. The unprinted film is as clear as a window and nearly invisible once pressed down on glass. Matte clear is slightly frosted, which softens the effect, so for bottles and jars we recommend gloss unless glare is a real problem.

faqs.q: Why do my colors look washed out on clear stickers?
faqs.a: Because CMYK inks are translucent and the surface behind them shows through. We fix that by printing a white ink layer under the colored areas, which gives the inks a solid base. The proof shows the white layer so you can check which areas get it.

faqs.q: Can clear stickers go on the inside of a window to face out?
faqs.a: Yes. We print the design mirrored and put the adhesive on the printed face, so you stick it to the inside of the glass and read it correctly from the street. It stays out of the rain and lasts longer than an outside application.

faqs.q: Do clear stickers survive the dishwasher on glass and tumblers?
faqs.a: Laminated clear vinyl handles the top rack of a home dishwasher for repeated cycles. Unlaminated prints eventually dull at the edges. For commercial dishwashers with high heat, we move you to clear PET, which tolerates heat and detergent better than vinyl.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum quantity for custom clear stickers?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 per design, the same as every material we print. At that count the price starts at $0.30 per sticker and includes free FedEx delivery in the United States. Separate designs can share one order if each hits 100.

faqs.q: Can I get custom clear decals for a car window?
faqs.a: Yes. Rear and side windows take a laminated clear vinyl decal applied on the outside, or a face-adhesive version applied inside. We recommend inside application for anything the rear wiper passes over, and a white ink layer so the design reads against tinted glass.

faqs.q: Will a clear sticker peel off a bottle in the fridge?
faqs.a: Not if the bottle was clean and dry when you applied it. Condensation after application does not weaken the adhesive. Condensation before application does, so label bottles at room temperature and let them sit an hour before chilling.

faqs.q: What is the difference between clear vinyl and clear PET stickers?
faqs.a: Clear vinyl is softer and wraps curved bottles easily, and it is the default. Clear PET is stiffer, clearer and tolerates heat, solvents and repeated scrubbing better, so it is the choice for lab bottles, equipment and anything going through high-temperature washing.

faqs.q: Can clear stickers be removed without leaving residue on glass?
faqs.a: With removable adhesive, yes, for about a year after application. Permanent adhesive on glass can still be removed with heat and a plastic scraper, then a wipe of isopropyl alcohol. Avoid metal blades on coated or tinted glass.

faqs.q: How small can text be on a custom clear sticker?
faqs.a: Keep white or light-colored text at 6 point or larger. The white ink underlayer is pulled in slightly from the color edge so it never peeks out, and on very thin strokes that can leave the text looking gray. Dark text on a clear base can go smaller.

faqs.q: Do custom transparent stickers come on a sheet or individually cut?
faqs.a: Either. Kiss cut sheets keep several stickers on one backing, which is easiest to hand out or mail. Individually cut pieces are better for labeling a production run. Rolls suit a label dispenser. Say which you need at the quote stage and the price adjusts.

faqs.q: Can you print a clear sticker with a partial white backing?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is one of the best tricks with clear film. Back the logo and text in white so they read solid, leave a tint or a line drawing unbacked so it takes on the color of the bottle. Mark the areas on the file or describe them and we build the layer.
